entities.name: An-Nadhar bin Syamil
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
An-Nadhar bin Syamil was an Arab scholar and poet from central Asia active in Iraq.

Born in unknown year and died in 818 CE, Abu ʾl-Ḥasan al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl ibn Kharasha al-Māzinī al-Tamīmī played a pivotal role in preserving classical knowledge and literary works during the medieval period.

His significance extends to the transmission of cultural heritage, as he was part of a network of scholars who contributed to the preservation of Arabic manuscripts.

A testament to his enduring legacy, An-Nadhar bin Syamil's works continue to influence contemporary scholarship and literary analysis.

In a striking example of the power of knowledge transmission, An-Nadhar bin Syamil's writings on classical poetry have been rediscovered and reinterpreted by modern scholars, offering a unique window into the intellectual traditions of the medieval Islamic world.
